run: 6 hours from nm25 on the RTX PRO 6000 with --early 0.25, as registered; 5,069 M hands at the end

2 the gain (early stage).result: difference with nm43 ahead after 15,000 deals: +3.24 bb/100, z +4.30 (boundary 3.80)

4 robustness.result: 30-minute exploiter +2.1 [+1.2, +2.9] (readings +1.0, +0.7, +2.1); the limit was nm25's +0.2 plus 1, i.e. +1.2

verdict: not adopted: check 4 fails. nm43 is better early in a tournament (+3.2 bb/100) and equal in nm25's game, but its exploiter wins more than the registered limit.
notes: The exploiter played nm43's own game (a quarter early tables), nm25's reference +0.2 was measured in nm25's game; the registration accepted that comparison and it stands.

nm41 (+1.6) and nm42 (+1.2) also read above +1.2: every network fine-tuned from nm25 has read above nm25's single +0.2, which may itself be a low draw. A fair comparison (both exploited in the same game, several seeds) would be a new registration, not a re-reading of this one.
nm43 does not call all-ins wider: facing one on early tables it folds 59% (nm25 47%), and against a jam-any bluffer 73% (nm25 71%). Its early-stage gain comes from elsewhere in its play.
